items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: And we had Joe Johnson on guitar. ... See he didn't make it on trumpet, so Roy switched the trombone and Joe went to trumpet.

ctx.x: Smoke stacks used to go, yeah. Yeah.

And we picked up another clarinet player out of Donistonville. I don't know what that boy was named. He was very good. You see, but it was a funny thing about all those guys on there, what we, what we thought we could play, we followed way late, there wasn't no way. Didn't we, man? That's right. Mm-hmm. That's right. You see, because we was in one band playing around with the other guys, they was some big shots, but way late we found them out. Yeah. See. See. Now, you know, you talk about your trumpet players, we…
And Joe Johnson was on the boat too then.

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: He had left working for McCall's and he started working with a little band, a guy called Roy Palmer... And Joe Johnson was our guitar player.

ctx.x: It was around 1997 and 1999 when my brother bought that big bass for me. Uh-huh. He had left working for McCall's and he started working with a little band, a guy called Roy Palmer. Roy Palmer, yes. Roy Palmer was our guitar player. You had to see what became a trombone player? No, let me see what Roy was playing. Roy was playing trumpet. Uh-huh. And Joe Johnson was our guitar player. So Joe Johnson learned trumpet and Roy Palmer and Roy Palmer was good too. Joe died. That's what I tell the guys, they read about…
Sure. Why would you play? Bass drum?
